messages:
Olivia: quick q — should the rerank response include a per-candidate model tag and a latency estimate? thinking about routing + cost visibility :thinking:
Raj: +1 for model tag, helps explainability and fallback routing decisions
Kim: latency estimate per candidate feels weird — estimates can be noisy. what's the use-case?
Olivia: product asks for UI that shows why results changed after a model swap. model tag answers that. latency is for console to highlight slow candidates and for cost accounting
Marta: for cost accounting we already have aggregate tokens/time metrics, but per-candidate latency could help spot outliers when a heavy model is used for certain candidates
Zach: implementation note: adding fields is fine but we must be careful about payload size. client sends 100 candidates today. per-candidate extra fields multiply quickly
Raj: proposal: add optional fields on a v2 envelope: "model_tag" and "exec_ms_estimate". mark as nullable and keep v1 unchanged. servers can omit to save bytes
Kim: can we compress exec_ms_estimate to a small int (ms) and model_tag as short enum id? then console maps id->display name
Olivia: yeah enum id + mapping is fine. but enums require service-managed registry + migration plan
Marta: telemetry question: what events do we emit? per-call summary and optional per-candidate sample? per-candidate for every call will be high-cardinality
analytics-bot: suggestion: emit per-call histogram of exec_ms and a sampled per-candidate event (1% by default) with model_tag and candidate_index
Zach: routing impact: if we include model_tag, downstream routing logic can prefer cheaper variants. need auth checks so customers can't force model hints to bypass pricing
Raj: security note — model_tag must be considered an informational hint, not a policy enforcer unless verified by server. otherwise a client could lie
Olivia: agreed. server should set model_tag based on actual model used in serving path. client-supplied hints should be separate field and never trusted for routing
Kim: rollout plan: feature-gate via response version header + console toggle. default v1 for 2 weeks, then soft enable 10% tenants, collect telemetry
Marta: console UX: show a small badge on results: "served-by: <model short name> (" ) with hover for latency percentile. only show when model_tag present
Zach: quota concerns: if downstream logic fans out to heavy models per candidate, cost skyrockets. we should add a server-side heuristic: if req.candidates > 50 and model is heavy, limit fanout or require explicit tenant opt-in
Raj: we also need quota meters: count "rerank_heavy_model_candidate" units per candidate served by heavy model. tie to existing quota dashboard
Olivia: agree. action items:
- Raj: define response envelope v2 schema (model_id enum, exec_ms as int) and compat rules (due EOD)
- Kim: config toggle + rollout plan for console + feature flag
- Marta: telemetry sampling spec and dashboard changes
- Zach: quota meter + routing heuristics
- analytics-bot: add event names: rerank.v2_response, rerank.candidate_sample, rerank.heavy_candidate_count
Raj: I'll draft schema. quick question: what about signed model provenance (hash) for audits? maybe overkill for now
Olivia: keep provenance optional in v2 as long string. mark as "audit_only" without UI surface for now
deploy-bot: canary deployed rerank-service v2 to cluster-a at 1707778920 :rocket:
Kim: sweet, let's monitor error rate and payload size. will post dashboard link when ready
Marta: logging note: redact model internal tags for public tenants (map to generic categories)
Olivia: thanks everyone. Raj — ping when schema PR is up and we'll schedule a short sync. :thumbsup:
